recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If the work group wants a comprehensive safety audit of all invariant and SearchParameter FHIRPath expressions, treat that as a separate human/tooling review rather than a remaining FHIR-48379 source edit.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive FHIR-I R6 clarification to warn that maximum cardinality changes can break FHIRPath expressions as well as JSON paths, including two version-management wording changes, a FHIRPath dragons warning, and an editor check of existing FHIRPath expressions.
initial_application: Brian Postlethwaite's 2025-10-22 FHIR-48379 commits 8a7bd856e19a1d222c350a911db3c04ecedd73f7 and cfbe4bd6c9435ec8643117cf43176e83a8a9b378, linked from Jira via HL7/fhir#3797, added the FHIRPath dragons warning to source/fhirpath.html and changed source/versions.html from JSON-only wording to JSON-and-FHIRPath wording.
additional_context: FHIR-I WGM minutes page 281219681 records the same 26-0-0 persuasive vote and notes that cardinality changes may break FHIRPath. FHIR-47629 is the same change family because it introduced the previous JSON-only cardinality warning; FHIR-47643 was checked because FHIR-48379 mentions it, but that snapshot concerns a different versions-page draft-resource reference rule. Zulip searches found no directly relevant or conflicting thread.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/versions.html already contains both approved FHIRPath-related edits and source/fhirpath.html already contains the requested dragons warning. The broad request to have an editor check invariants and SearchParameter definitions did not identify a concrete current source defect in the issue evidence.
